activation_method: CO2 physical activation at 855 °C for 20 h in a vertical tube furnace (235 mL/min CO2; 0.52 g bed); burn-off 65 wt%, BO/t 3.23 wt%/h
source_location: main p.6, Fig. 3a, series CS-855-65 (red diamonds)
notes: archive: HYC-0076_fig3a_CS-855-65.json. Low-pressure marker: pressure resolution about 0.3 bar per pixel. Other markers of this isotherm not extracted: markers at ~3, 4 and 5 bar overlap each other and the CS-865-66/CS-835-52 markers and were not separable. Hiden XEMIS gravimetric analyser; degassed in situ at 200 °C (10 °C/min) for 4 h; sample mass "at least 50 mg" loaded (dry weight >20 mg), not stated exactly; H2 BIP+ (Air Products), purity not given as a number; base vacuum <1e-6 mbar (instrument, not stated as degas end pressure). Characterization (Table 3): A_BET 2451 m2/g (N2 at -196 °C, Micromeritics ASAP 2020, BET via BETSI software; P/P0 range and consistency criteria not stated); Vp 1.06 cm3/g = single-point total pore volume at p/p0 0.95 (N2); Vmicro (<2 nm) 0.94, V<1nm 0.45 (stored as ultramicropore volume, cutoff 1 nm), V<50nm 1.0 cm3/g from 2D-NLDFT heterogeneous-surface kernel dual fit to N2 and H2 (-196 °C, 1 bar) isotherms (SAIEUS). Composition (Table S1, elemental analysis): N 2.79 wt%, O 2.83 wt%. Class doped_carbon: N (~3 wt%) from the triethylenediamine crosslinker is built into the carbon and discussed as N-doping retained after CO2 activation. | C: single digitization (B only); uncertainty 1% of the uptake-axis span.
extractor: dual extraction A (claude-sonnet-5-5) and B (claude-opus-5-5), reconciled by C (claude-opus-5-5)
basis_evidence: All isotherms and reported uptake data in this work are in terms of total adsorption. This must be derived from the measured, net isotherm by accounting for the skeletal density and pore volume of the adsorbent [23]. Net uptake isotherms were converted to excess uptake isotherms using skeletal (He) densities as measured on a Micromeritics Accupyc II. ... Conversion from excess to total uptake isotherm was then performed using the single point total pore volume determined in Section 2.2.
free_volume_calibration: buoyancy (net-to-excess) correction using skeletal He density measured on Micromeritics AccuPyc II at room temperature

activation_method: CO2 physical activation at 855 C for 20 h (0.52 g CS, CO2 235 mL/min), burn-off 65 %
source_location: main.pdf p.6 Fig. 3a, series CS-855-65 (red diamonds), lowest marker (on the y-axis)
notes: C: row added by the reconciler: value from B archive HYC-0076_fig3a_CS-855-65.json point 1 (x -0.018 bar, y 0.8794 wt%), for which B wrote no row; A did not digitize markers of this series below 10 bar. Marker sits on the y-axis (digitized pressure below the ~0.3 bar/pixel resolution), so pressure_bar empty with pressure_unstated true, as for the matching first markers of CS-885-82 and CS-865-66. Single digitization; uncertainty 1% of axis span. | BET: N2 77 K, BETSI software, P/p0 range not stated. Vp: single-point N2 at p/p0 0.95. Vmicro (<2 nm) and V<1nm (ultramicropore volume, 1 nm cutoff): dual N2+H2 2D-NLDFT heterogeneous kernel (SAIEUS). Printed: ABET 2451, Vp 1.06, Vmicro 0.94, V<1nm 0.45, V<50nm 1.00 cm3/g. N 2.79 wt% (SI Table S1, elemental analysis). Hiden XEMIS H2 BIP+ (Air Products, purity not stated); loaded mass at least 50 mg (dry >20 mg), not a single value.
extractor: dual extraction A (claude-sonnet-5-5) and B (claude-opus-5-5), reconciled by C (claude-opus-5-5)
basis_evidence: All isotherms and reported uptake data in this work are in terms of total adsorption. This must be derived from the measured, net isotherm by accounting for the skeletal density and pore volume of the adsorbent [23]. Net uptake isotherms were converted to excess uptake isotherms using skeletal (He) densities as measured on a Micromeritics Accupyc II. ... Conversion from excess to total uptake isotherm was then performed using the single point total pore volume determined in Section 2.2.
free_volume_calibration: buoyancy correction from He skeletal density (Micromeritics Accupyc II, room temperature)

title: Sustainable and synthetic carbon polymers for safe and efficient H2 storage
material_description: CS-865-79 | N-containing carbon microspheres: phloroglucinol/glyoxylic acid polymer microspheres crosslinked with triethylenediamine (microwave-assisted sol-gel, 50 °C, 2.5 h), carbonized at 850 °C under N2, then CO2-activated at 865 °C for 23 h (burn-off 79 wt%)
activation_method: CO2 physical activation at 865 °C for 23 h in a vertical tube furnace (235 mL/min CO2; 0.52 g bed); burn-off 79 wt%, BO/t 3.45 wt%/h
source_location: SI p.8, Fig. S8b, series CS-865-79 (grey diamonds), highest-pressure point of the predicted -123 °C isotherm
notes: C: row added by the reconciler (neither extraction digitized this endpoint; the grey diamond is fully visible). Digitized with digitize_figure.py (markers mode) on in/pages/si1-8.png after isolating the marker; calibration x 50/150 bar at px 795.5/1034.5 (check 100 bar at 915.5), y 1/5 wt% at px 1184/851 (check 3 wt% at 1017.5); archive work/dig/HYC-0076_figS8b_CS-865-79_C.json (unchecked: no printed value on this curve within the plotted range). Single digitization; uncertainty 1% of axis span. Predicted (Clausius-Clapeyron/Toth potential) isotherm, not measured. The endpoints of CS-845-64 (S8a), CS-835-78 and CS-845-79 (S8b) are hidden behind other markers and were not digitized.
extractor: dual extraction A (claude-sonnet-5-5) and B (claude-opus-5-5), reconciled by C (claude-opus-5-5)
basis_evidence: All isotherms and reported uptake data in this work are in terms of total adsorption. This must be derived from the measured, net isotherm by accounting for the skeletal density and pore volume of the adsorbent [23]. Net uptake isotherms were converted to excess uptake isotherms using skeletal (He) densities as measured on a Micromeritics Accupyc II. [...] Conversion from excess to total uptake isotherm was then performed using the single point total pore volume determined in Section 2.2. (main p.3, Section 2.3)
free_volume_calibration: buoyancy (net-to-excess) correction using skeletal He density measured on Micromeritics AccuPyc II at room temperature
